questions.question: A rocket is launched straight upward from the surface of a planet that has no atmosphere. The rocket very quickly reaches escape velocity. At that instant, the rocket’s engine turns off. After a long time, as the rocket moves farther away from the planet, what happens to the rocket’s speed, and what reasoning supports the claim?
questions.title: Escape velocity - what happens to speed

options.text: The speed approaches zero. As the rocket moves farther away from the planet, both the potential energy of the rocket-planet system and kinetic energy of the rocket approach zero.
The speed approaches zero. Even if the rocket moves beyond the planet’s gravity there must always be a force from the engine to keep it moving.
The speed approaches a positive value. Once the rocket is beyond the planet’s gravity its speed remains constant because the net force on it is zero.
The speed approaches a positive value. The potential energy of the rocket-planet system is increasing, and the rocket’s kinetic energy is already a positive value.

questions.question: A small box is on a ramp inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal. The box may be subject to the following forces: The force of friction F f , the normal force F N , the gravitational force F g , and an external pushing force F P . Forces in Figures 1 and 2 are drawn such that their lengths are proportional to their magnitudes. [图: Two figures are shown. Each figure shows a small box on a ramp inclined upward and to the right at an angle of theta from the horizontal. In each figure, the box is subject to multiple forces. In figure 1, a medium sized arrow labeled F sub N extends upward and to the left from the top of the box, perpendicular to the incline of the ramp. A short arrow labeled F sub lowercase f extends upward and to the right from the right side of the box, parallel to the incline of the ramp. A medium size arrow labeled F sub g extends vertically downward from the bottom side of the box. In figure 2, a medium sized arrow labeled F sub N extends upward and to the left from the top of the box, perpendicular to the incline of the ramp. A long arrow labeled F sub P extends upward and to the right from the right side of the box, parallel to the incline of the ramp. A medium size arrow labeled F sub g extends vertically downward from the bottom side of the box. A short arrow labeled F sub lowercase f extends downward and to the left from the left side of the box, parallel to the incline of the ramp.] If the acceleration is directed up the ramp, which figure best represents the free-body diagram for the box and what evidence supports the claim?
questions.title: Free-body diagram - which figure accelerates up

options.text: Figure 1 : There is nothing opposing the force of friction that is directed up the ramp.
Figure 1 : For friction to be directed up the ramp, the box must be sliding down the ramp, and therefore its speed is decreasing.
Figure 2 : Any amount of force pushing the object up the ramp would cause it to accelerate in that direction.
Figure 2 : The pushing force is greater in magnitude than friction and the component of gravity parallel to the ramp.
